clue.text: Not abridged, containing nothing hot or vulgar

indicators.note: containing tells us the uncut word holds the other two pieces inside it

parts.note: a text that is not abridged is uncut
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A complaint that an unabridged book still has nothing spicy or crude in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone uncouth is coarse and ill-mannered, which is a synonym of vulgar.

clue.text: Encouraged — lost canoe, but still encouraged!

indicators.note: lost says the canoe's letters go missing from the first word, the rest rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cheered on despite losing their canoe.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the letters C, A, N, O, E from ENCOURAGED and URGED is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To be urged is to be pressed or encouraged to act, a synonym.

clue.text: Interlinked cap and hat with which I made bread

indicators.note: interlinked suggests the two headwear words are tangled together, so rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone baking with a cap and hat joined together.
explanation.walkthrough: CAP and HAT rearranged give CHAPAT, then I.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened Indian bread.

clue.text: An integral component of munitions

indicators.note: of indicates that the answer is a piece taken from within the word munitions

explanation.surface: A remark that something is an essential part of an arsenal.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single component forming part of a whole.

clue.text: Man turned fuel to money and island state to metropolis at 12's suggestion

parts.note: he is a man, the male pronoun

indicators.note: turned means the word for fuel is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: oil is a fuel
a cent is a coin, a small piece of money
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island, a US state
a city is a metropolis

explanation.surface: A man turning fuel into cash and a state into a city, on Copernicus's advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 12 is COPERNICUS, who suggested the sun is the centre of the solar system; 'to' and 'and' simply join pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Heliocentricity, the sun-centred system, was the model Copernicus proposed.

clue.text: Leave the country, making note sound discordant

parts.note: mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale
to grate is to make a harsh, jarring noise

explanation.surface: A musician leaving the country after hitting a sour note.
explanation.definitionFit: To migrate is to move away from one's homeland to settle elsewhere, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Paper about flower and ship by island expert

indicators.note: about says the paper goes around the flower and ship

parts.note: MS is a manuscript, a paper
the aster is a daisy-like flower
craft means a boat or ship
Man is the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A paper written about a flower and a ship near an island, by an expert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' looks like a river here, but it is the bloom ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A master craftsman is a highly skilled artisan, so an expert.

clue.text: Naive sort of music with potentially catastrophic effect

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
house is a style of electronic dance music

explanation.surface: Naive dance music that might have dire consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the greenhouse effect, warming the planet, is potentially catastrophic.
explanation.definitionFit: The greenhouse effect is the global warming feared to be catastrophic, so the word goes with that effect.

clue.text: Gold staple pinning plate to ear

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: pinning has the staple hold the plate inside it

parts.note: rice is a staple food
the L-plate, shown by learner drivers, gives L

explanation.surface: A gold staple fixing a plate to someone's ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staple' suggests a metal fastener but is a staple food, RICE.
explanation.definitionFit: The auricle is the outer visible part of the ear.

clue.text: Oriental pushes off to ancient city

parts.note: E stands for eastern, oriental

indicators.note: off suggests the word pushes has gone wrong, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone from the East pushing off on a trip to an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was an ancient Greek city in Asia Minor, now in Turkey.

clue.text: Relieved student in credit notes bloom

parts.note: relieved means glad

indicators.note: in places the student's letter inside the run of credit notes

parts.note: IOUs are written promises to pay, notes acknowledging credit
L is a learner, as on the L-plate, standing for a student

explanation.surface: A student relieved to be in credit after receiving some notes, pictured as blooming.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a garden flower, so it is an example of a bloom.

clue.text: See 14
Wanting life to be exact

definitions.meaning: lacking life, as in no longer living
precise, as in ... centre or ... on time

explanation.definitionFit: Dead means lifeless, and also means precise or absolute, as in a dead heat.

clue.text: Firm, injurious, losing 1-0 to champion of 4

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: losing says the score's figures are taken out of the injurious word

parts.note: pernicious means harmful or injurious
the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A football team losing a damaging match one-nil.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1-0 scoreline is read as the letters I and O, removed from PERNICIOUS to leave PERNICUS. 4 is HELIOCENTRICITY, the sun-centred model.
explanation.definitionFit: The astronomer Copernicus proposed the sun-centred model of the solar system, so he championed it.

clue.text: Referee may notice Hardy hero embracing Italy fan

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: embracing means the hero's name goes round Italy and the fan

parts.note: Jude the Obscure is the hero of Thomas Hardy's novel
I is the international vehicle code for Italy
cat is jazz slang for a fan or devotee

explanation.surface: A referee spotting one of Hardy's heroes hugging an Italian supporter.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjudicate is to judge or referee a dispute, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Tolkien setting the converse of 4?

definitions.meaning: the fictional world in which Tolkien set his Hobbit and Lord of the Rings stories
4 places the sun at the centre; the converse puts our planet in the ... instead

explanation.walkthrough: 4 is HELIOCENTRICITY; its converse is a planet-centred universe, read here literally as the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolkien's legendarium is set on a continent of that name, and the phrase read literally describes a geocentric universe.

clue.text: Look determined in Lewis's cupboards

indicators.note: in places the look and determined pieces inside the Lewis initials

parts.note: C. S. Lewis, author of the Narnia books, gives his initials CS
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
set means fixed or determined

explanation.surface: Seeing something decided inside the wardrobes of C. S. Lewis, famed for a magic wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Closets are small rooms or cupboards for storing things, a synonym.

clue.text: Revolt in Hell? Blast!

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, another name for Hell
a gust is a blast of wind

explanation.surface: An uprising in the underworld, met with an exclamation of annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: To revolt someone is to sicken or repel them, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Silly sod kept publishing (sort of)

indicators.note: silly suggests the words are muddled, so rearranged

explanation.surface: Calling someone a silly fool for keeping something.
explanation.walkthrough: Desktop publishing is producing documents on a personal computer, a sort of publishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Desktop is a sort of publishing, laying out documents on a computer, so the word completes that phrase.

clue.text: Headless horseman disturbed the resort

indicators.note: disturbed means the remaining letters are shaken up and rearranged
headless means the word horseman loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A headless rider upsetting a holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: San Remo is a seaside resort on the Italian Riviera.

clue.text: When to indicate or appoint

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
to sign is to signal or indicate

explanation.surface: A question about when to point something out or name someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To assign someone is to appoint them to a task or post, a synonym.

clue.text: One prisoner raised sign to champion of 4

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the pieces read upwards, so reversed

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
lag is slang for a convict, as in old lag
Leo is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: A prisoner lifting a sign to support a cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is HELIOCENTRICITY; Galileo was tried for supporting it, which makes 'prisoner' apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Galileo defended the sun-centred model and was punished for it, so he championed it.

clue.text: Revolutionary racket is interrupting gift-bearer

indicators.note: interrupting puts the racket and is inside the gift-bearer, splitting him

parts.note: Santa Claus brings gifts at Christmas
din is a loud noise, a racket

explanation.surface: A noisy disturbance breaking in on Father Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sandinistas were the revolutionary movement that took power in Nicaragua in 1979.

clue.text: Almost crumble in fire

indicators.note: almost means the word for crumble is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to flake is to crumble into small pieces

explanation.surface: Something nearly falling apart inside a blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Flak is anti-aircraft gunfire, from a German abbreviation, so it is a kind of fire.

clue.text: Canoe unaffected by capsizing

indicators.note: a word unchanged when turned upside down in a down clue reads the same backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A boat that is not harmed when it rolls over.
explanation.definitionFit: A kayak is a kind of canoe paddled with a double-bladed paddle.

clue.text: Feature of fingerboard causes worry

definitions.meaning: a raised ridge across the neck of a guitar marking where notes fall

explanation.definitionFit: A fret is a guitar's ridge; to fret is to worry.

clue.text: Letter of thanks appended to article

indicators.note: appended to puts the thanks piece on after the article

parts.note: the is the definite article
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A thank-you letter attached to a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Compiler's taking little time to recover by foul means

parts.note: the compiler is the setter, so compiler's is I'm, short for I am
mo is short for moment, a little time
to rally is to recover strength

explanation.surface: A crossword setter taking a moment to recover after behaving badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something immorally means doing it wickedly or by foul means, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Employ model that's wrong — his didn't involve 4

indicators.note: that's wrong signals that the letters are put together incorrectly, so rearranged

parts.note: the Model T was Henry Ford's famous car

explanation.surface: Using a model that turns out to be wrong, as the ancient astronomer did.
explanation.walkthrough: 4 is HELIOCENTRICITY: Ptolemy's model put the earth, not the sun, at the centre, so the wrong model is part of the joke.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy's astronomical system was earth-centred, so his model did not involve a sun-centred universe.

clue.text: Fishermen's labour organisation?

parts.note: a net is the fisherman's tool, his possession
labour means work

explanation.surface: Questioning whether fishermen's work counts as an organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: A network is an interconnected system or organisation, as of contacts or broadcasters.
